units.zh: 姚顗，字伯真，京兆萬年人。
units.en: Yao Yi, courtesy name Bozhen, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Yao Yi, style name Bozhen, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 曾祖希齊，湖州司功參軍。
units.en: His great-grandfather Xiqi served as staff merit officer in Huzhou.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Xiqi was Merit Officer on the staff of Huzhou.

units.zh: 祖宏慶，蘇州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Hongqing was prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: His grandfather Hongqing was Prefect of Suzhou.

units.zh: 父荊，國子祭酒。
units.en: His father Jing served as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
units.literal: His father Jing was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 顗少蠢，敦厚，靡事容貌，任其自然，流輩未之重，唯兵部侍郎司空圖深器之，以女妻焉。
units.en: As a young man Yi seemed slow and unpolished, yet he was honest and steadfast, paid little heed to his looks, and let things be. His contemporaries did not think much of him, but Vice Minister of War Sikong Tu recognized his worth and married his daughter to him.
units.literal: Yi in youth was dull and simple, honest and thick; he cared nothing for his appearance and let nature take its course. His peers did not esteem him; only Vice Minister of War Sikong Tu greatly valued him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

units.zh: 顗性仁恕，多為仆妾所欺，心雖察之，而不能面折，終身無喜怒。
units.en: Yi was gentle and forbearing by nature. Servants and concubines often took advantage of him; he saw through their tricks but could never bring himself to confront them openly, and he never showed anger or delight throughout his life.
units.literal: Yi was by nature benevolent and forgiving; he was often deceived by servants and concubines. Though he perceived it in his heart, he could not reproach them to their faces, and throughout his life he showed neither anger nor joy.

units.zh: 不知錢百之為陌，黍百之為銖，凡家人市貨百物，入增其倍，出減其半，不詢其由，無擔石之儲，心不隕獲。
units.en: He did not even know that a hundred cash make a string or a hundred grains of millet make a measure. Whenever the household bought or sold goods, they doubled prices on purchases and cut them in half on sales, and he never asked why. He had scarcely a bushel of grain in store, yet he never fretted over his losses.
units.literal: He did not know that a hundred coins make a string or that a hundred grains of millet make a zhu. Whenever household members bought or sold anything, they doubled the price on what came in and halved it on what went out, without his asking why. He had no stores of grain worth even a dan or shi, yet his heart never fell to despair over gain.

units.zh: 唐末，隨計入洛，出遊嵩山，有白衣丈夫拜於路側，請為童仆。
units.en: Late in the Tang he traveled to Luoyang for the civil service examination. On an outing to Mount Song, a man dressed in white bowed to him beside the road and asked to become his attendant.
units.literal: In the late Tang he went to Luoyang for the provincial examination; while touring Mount Song he met a man in white robes who bowed by the roadside and asked to serve as his page.

units.zh: 顗辭不納。
units.en: Yi refused and would not take him in.
units.literal: Yi declined and would not accept him.

units.zh: 乃曰：「鬼神享於德，君子孚於信。
units.en: The man then said, "Spirits feast on virtue, and the gentleman lives by good faith.
units.literal: The man then said: "Spirits and ghosts feast upon virtue; the gentleman rests upon trust.

units.zh: 余則鬼也，將以托賢者之德，通化工之信，幸無辭焉。
units.en: I am a ghost, and I wish to rely on the virtue of a worthy man and share in the faith that moves heaven and earth. I beg you not to turn me away.
units.literal: I am a ghost, and wish to entrust myself to the virtue of a worthy man and join in the trust of transforming creation—please do not refuse.

units.zh: 昔余掌事陰府，承命攝人之魂氣，名氏同而其人非，且富有壽算，復而歸之，則筋骸已敗，由是獲譴，使不得為陽生。
units.en: Long ago I held office in the realm of the dead and was charged to take charge of people's souls. When the name matched but the person did not, and the allotted span of life was still long, restoring the soul would find the body already decayed. For this I was condemned and barred from returning to life among men.
units.literal: Formerly I managed affairs in the yin realm and received orders to seize people's vital breath. When the name was the same but the person was not, and the allotted span was still long, if I returned the breath the flesh would already be ruined. For this I was punished and forbidden to live again among the living.

units.zh: 公中夏之相輔也，今為謁中天之祠，若以某姓名求之，神必許諾。」
units.en: You are destined to be a chief minister of the Central Realm. Go now and offer prayers at the central shrine of Heaven; if you petition in a certain name, the spirits will surely assent."
units.literal: You will be a chief minister of the Central Plain. Now go pay your respects at the shrine of Heaven in the Central Plain; if you pray using a certain name, the spirits will surely grant it."

units.zh: 顗因為之虔禱而還，白衣迎於山下，曰：「余免其苦矣。」
units.en: Yi prayed earnestly for him and returned. The man in white greeted him at the foot of the mountain and said, "I have been released from my torment."
units.literal: Yi therefore prayed devoutly on his behalf and returned. The man in white met him at the foot of the mountain and said: "I am freed from my suffering."

units.zh: 拜謝而退。
units.en: He bowed in gratitude and departed.
units.literal: He bowed in thanks and withdrew.

units.zh: 顗次年擢進士第。
units.en: The following year Yi passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: The next year Yi passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 梁貞明中，歷校書郎、登封令、右補闕、禮部員外郎，召入翰林，累遷至中書舍人。
units.en: During the Liang Zhenming era he held successive posts as collator, magistrate of Dengfeng, Right Reminder, and vice director of the Ministry of Rites, then was called into the Hanlin Academy and eventually rose to Secretariat drafter.
units.literal: In the Zhenming era of Liang he served successively as collator, magistrate of Dengfeng, Right Reminder, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy and rose in stages to Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，以例貶復州司馬，歲餘牽復，授左散騎常侍，歷兵吏部侍郎、尚書左丞。
units.en: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Yi was demoted under precedent to military adjutant of Fuzhou. After a year he was recalled and made Left Regular Attendant, then served as vice minister of war, vice minister of personnel, and left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Yi was demoted by precedent to military adjutant of Fuzhou; after more than a year he was recalled and appointed Left Regular Attendant, then served as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 唐末帝即位，講求輔相，乃書朝中清望官十餘人姓名置於瓶中，清夜焚香而挾之，既而得盧文紀與顗，遂拜中書侍郎、平章事。
units.en: When the last Tang emperor came to the throne he sought chief ministers. He wrote the names of a dozen eminent officials on slips, placed them in a bottle, burned incense on a clear night, and drew lots. Lu Wenji and Yi were chosen, and both were appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
units.literal: When the last Tang emperor took the throne he sought chief ministers; he wrote the names of more than ten officials of clear reputation in court on slips, placed them in a bottle, burned incense on a clear night, and drew them. He drew Lu Wenji and Yi, and thereupon appointed them Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 制前一日，嵩山白衣來謁，謂顗曰：「公明日為相。」
units.en: On the eve of the appointment edict, the man in white from Mount Song came to see Yi and said, "Tomorrow you will become chief minister."
units.literal: On the day before the edict, the man in white from Mount Song came to visit Yi and said: "Tomorrow you will become chief minister."

units.zh: 其言無差，冥數固先定矣。
units.en: His words proved exact; what was ordained in the unseen world had been settled long before.
units.literal: His words were not in error; fate in the unseen realm had indeed been fixed beforehand.

units.zh: 高祖登極，罷相為刑部尚書，俄遷戶部尚書。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he removed Yi from the chief ministership and appointed him minister of justice, then soon made him minister of revenue.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he removed Yi from the chief ministership and made him Minister of Justice, soon transferring him to Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 天福五年冬卒，年七十五。
units.en: He died in the winter of the fifth Tianfu year, at the age of seventy-five.
units.literal: He died in winter of the fifth year of Tianfu, aged seventy-five.

units.zh: 贈左僕射。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 子惟和嗣。
units.en: His son Weihe succeeded to his line.
units.literal: His son Weihe succeeded him.

units.zh: 顗疏於財，而禦家無術，既死，斂葬之資不備，家人俟賻物及鬻第方能舉喪而去。
units.en: Yi was indifferent to money and inept at running his household. When he died there was not enough for burial; his family had to wait for gifts of condolence and the sale of the house before they could hold the funeral and leave.
units.literal: Yi was careless with wealth and had no skill in managing the household. After his death the funds for burial were not ready; his family had to wait for condolence gifts and the sale of the residence before they could conduct the funeral and depart.

units.zh: 士大夫愛其廉而鄙其拙。
units.en: Men of letters admired his integrity but looked down on his lack of practical sense.
units.literal: The scholar-officials admired his integrity but despised his dullness.

units.zh: 呂琦，字輝山，幽州安次人也。
units.en: Lü Qi, courtesy name Huishan, was a native of Anci in Youzhou.
units.literal: Lü Qi, style name Huishan, was a man of Anci in Youzhou.

units.zh: 祖壽，瀛州景城主簿。
units.en: His grandfather Shou served as recorder of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.
units.literal: His grandfather Shou was Recorder of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.

units.zh: 父兗，滄州節度判官，累至檢校右庶子。
units.en: His father Yan was military adjutant on the Cangzhou circuit and eventually rose to acting Right Household Companion.
units.literal: His father Yan was military adjutant of Cangzhou and rose in stages to Acting Right Household Companion.

units.zh: 劉守光攻陷滄州，琦父兗被擒，族之。
units.en: When Liu Shouguang seized Cangzhou, Qi's father Yan was captured and the entire clan was put to death.
units.literal: When Liu Shouguang captured Cangzhou, Qi's father Yan was taken and his clan exterminated.

units.zh: 琦時年十五，為吏追攝，將就戮焉。
units.en: Qi was only fifteen. Officials pursued and seized him, and he was on the point of execution.
units.literal: Qi was then fifteen; officials pursued and seized him, and he was about to be executed.

units.zh: 有趙玉者，幽、薊之義士也，久遊於兗之門下，見琦臨危，乃紿謂監者曰：「此子某之同氣也，幸無濫焉。」
units.en: A man named Zhao Yu, a champion of You and Ji who had long been attached to Yan's household, saw Qi in mortal danger. He tricked the guard, saying, "This boy is my own brother—please do not harm him wantonly."
units.literal: There was a Zhao Yu, a man of honor from You and Ji who had long been a guest in Yan's household. Seeing Qi in peril, he deceived the guard, saying: "This boy is my own kin—please do not kill him indiscriminately."

units.zh: 監者信之，即引之俱去。
units.en: The guard believed him and let them leave together.
units.literal: The guard believed him and led them both away together.

units.zh: 行一舍，琦困於徒步，以足病告，玉負之而行，逾數百里，因變姓名，乞食於路，乃免其禍。
units.en: After one day's march Qi could go no farther on foot and pleaded a foot ailment. Yu carried him on his back for hundreds of miles. They changed their names and begged along the road, and so escaped disaster.
units.literal: After traveling one stage, Qi was exhausted on foot and pleaded foot ailment. Yu carried him on his back for several hundred li. They changed their names and begged food along the road, and thus escaped the calamity.

units.zh: 年弱冠，以家門遇禍，邈無所依，乃勵志勤學，多遊於汾、晉。
units.en: In his early twenties, with his family destroyed and no one to turn to, he set his mind on study and traveled widely through Fen and Jin.
units.literal: When he reached young manhood, his family having met calamity and he with nowhere to rely upon, he resolved to study diligently and traveled widely in Fen and Jin.

units.zh: 唐天祐中，莊宗方開霸府，翹佇賢士，墨制授琦代州軍事判官，秩滿歸太原，監軍使張承業重琦器量，禮遇尤厚。
units.en: During the Tang Tianyou era Zhuangzong was establishing his headquarters and eagerly sought talented men. By special edict he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended Qi returned to Taiyuan, where Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye admired his character and treated him with exceptional regard.
units.literal: In the Tianyou era of Tang, Zhuangzong was opening his hegemon's office and eagerly awaited worthy men. By imperial order on black he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended he returned to Taiyuan; Military Commissioner Zhang Chengye valued Qi's capacity and treated him with exceptional courtesy.

units.zh: 天成初，拜琦殿中侍御史，遷駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事。
units.en: At the start of the Tiancheng era Qi was made attending censor in the palace, then promoted to vice director of the transport office while also serving as censor-in-chief of miscellaneous affairs.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Qi was appointed Attending Censor in the Palace and promoted to Vice Director of the Transport Office, concurrently serving as Censor-in-Chief of Miscellaneous Affairs.

units.zh: 會河陽帑吏竊財事發，詔軍巡院鞫之。
units.en: When a treasury clerk in Heyang was found to have embezzled funds, the court ordered the Military Patrol Office to investigate.
units.literal: When the theft of treasury funds by a clerk in Heyang came to light, an edict ordered the Military Patrol Office to investigate.

units.zh: 時軍巡使尹訓怙勢納賂，枉直相反，俄有訴冤於闕下者，詔琦按之，既驗其奸，乃上言請治尹訓，沮而不行。
units.en: The military patrol commissioner Yin Xun abused his power and took bribes, perverting justice. Soon a petitioner brought a grievance to the palace. Qi was ordered to investigate; once the fraud was confirmed he memorialized for Yin Xun's punishment, but the request was blocked.
units.literal: The Military Patrol Commissioner Yin Xun relied on power and accepted bribes, reversing right and wrong. Soon someone appealed injustice at the palace gates. Qi was ordered to investigate; having verified the wrongdoing, he submitted a memorial requesting punishment of Yin Xun, but it was blocked and not carried out.

units.zh: 琦連奏不已，訓知其不免，自殺於家，其獄遂明，蒙活者甚眾，自是朝廷多琦之公直。
units.en: Qi kept submitting memorials without letup. Xun knew he could not escape and killed himself at home. The case was finally cleared, and many who would have been condemned were spared. From then on the court widely praised Qi's integrity.
units.literal: Qi submitted memorial after memorial without cease. Xun knew he could not escape and killed himself at home. The case was then cleared, and very many who would have died were spared. From this the court greatly esteemed Qi's fairness and integrity.

units.zh: 高祖建義於太原，唐末帝幸懷州，趙德鈞駐軍於團柏谷，末帝以琦嘗在德鈞幕下，因令賫都統使官告以賜之，且犒其軍焉。
units.en: When Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor went to Huai Prefecture while Zhao Dejun camped at Tuanbai Valley. Because Qi had once served on Dejun's staff, the emperor sent him bearing the commander-in-chief's commission as a gift to Dejun and to reward his troops.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised righteous arms at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor went to Huai Prefecture and Zhao Dejun encamped at Tuanbai Valley. Because Qi had once served in Dejun's staff, the last emperor had him carry the commission of commander-in-chief to present to Dejun and also reward his army.

units.zh: 及觀軍於北陲，館於忻州，會晉祖降下晉安寨，遣使告於近郡，琦適遇其使，即斬之以聞，尋率郡兵千人間道而歸。
units.en: While inspecting troops on the northern frontier he was stationed at Xin Prefecture. The Jin founder had taken Jin'an Stockade and sent messengers to the neighboring prefectures. Qi happened upon one of them, executed him and reported it, then led a thousand local troops back by a secret route.
units.literal: When he went to review troops on the northern frontier he lodged at Xin Prefecture. The Jin founder had taken Jin'an Stockade and sent envoys to notify nearby prefectures. Qi happened upon one of the envoys, beheaded him and reported it, then led a thousand prefectural troops by a hidden route back.

units.zh: 高祖入洛，亦弗之責，止改授秘書監而已。
units.en: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not reproach him, but only reassigned him as director of the Palace Library.
units.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not blame him either, merely transferring him to Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 天福中，預修《唐書》，權掌選部，皆有能名焉。
units.en: During the Tianfu era he helped compile the History of Tang and held acting charge of the Selection Bureau, earning a name for competence in both.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era he took part in compiling the History of Tang and held acting charge of the Selection Bureau; in all these he won a reputation for ability.

units.zh: 累遷禮部、刑部、戶部、兵部侍郎，階至金紫光祿大夫，爵至開國子。
units.en: He rose through successive posts as vice minister of rites, justice, revenue, and war, attaining the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Viscount of a Founding State.
units.literal: He rose in stages to Vice Minister of Rites, Justice, Revenue, and War, reaching the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Baron of a founding state.

units.zh: 琦美風儀，有器概，雖以剛直聞於時，而內實仁恕。
units.en: Qi had a dignified presence and true breadth of character. Though famed in his day for uncompromising integrity, at heart he was gentle and forgiving.
units.literal: Qi had fine bearing and great capacity. Though known in his time for stern uprightness, inwardly he was truly benevolent and forgiving.

units.zh: 初，高祖謀求輔相，時宰臣李崧力薦琦於高祖，雲可大用。
units.en: When Gaozu was seeking chief ministers, Chief Minister Li Song strongly recommended Qi to him, saying he was fit for the highest office.
units.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu sought chief ministers, the chief minister Li Song strongly recommended Qi to Gaozu, saying he could be greatly employed.

units.zh: 高祖數召琦於便殿，言及當世事，甚奇之，方將倚以為相，忽遇疾而逝，人皆惜之。
units.en: Gaozu repeatedly summoned Qi to the informal hall to discuss affairs of state and came to admire him greatly. He was on the verge of making Qi chief minister when Qi suddenly fell ill and died. Everyone mourned the loss.
units.literal: Gaozu repeatedly summoned Qi to the informal hall and spoke of current affairs; he greatly admired him and was about to rely on him as chief minister, when Qi suddenly fell ill and died. All regretted it.

units.zh: 梁文矩，字德儀，鄆州人。
units.en: Liang Wenju, courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Yunzhou.
units.literal: Liang Wenju, style name Deyi, was a man of Yunzhou.

units.zh: 父景，秘書少監。
units.en: His father Jing served as vice director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: His father Jing was Vice Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 梁福王友璋好接賓客，文矩少遊其門，初試太子校書，轉秘書郎。
units.en: Prince Youzhang of Fu in Liang loved to entertain guests, and Wenju frequented his household as a young man. He first passed the examination for collator of the heir apparent, then became a secretary.
units.literal: Prince of Fu of Liang Youzhang loved to receive guests; Wenju in youth frequented his house. He first passed the examination for collator of the Heir Apparent, then became Secretary.

units.zh: 友璋領鄆州，奏為項城令，及移鎮徐方，辟為從事。
units.en: When Youzhang governed Yunzhou he recommended Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he transferred his command to Xuzhou he took Wenju on as an aide.
units.literal: When Youzhang held Yunzhou he memorialized Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng; when he moved his command to Xuzhou he recruited him as aide.

units.zh: 友璋卒，改兗州觀察判官。
units.en: After Youzhang's death Wenju became observation commissioner adjutant of Yanzhou.
units.literal: When Youzhang died, Wenju became observation commissioner adjutant of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 時莊宗遣明宗襲據鄆州，文矩以父母在鄆，一旦隔越，不知存亡，為子之情，戀望如灼，遂間路歸鄆，尋謁莊宗。
units.en: Zhuangzong had sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were there, and overnight he was cut off from them with no word of their fate. Filial longing burned in him, and he made his way back to Yun by a hidden route, then presented himself to Zhuangzong.
units.literal: At that time Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were in Yun; suddenly cut off, he did not know whether they lived or died. Filial feeling burned in him like fire, and he took a secret route back to Yun, then soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗喜之，授天平軍節度掌書記，在明宗幕下。
units.en: Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him secretary on the Tianping military commission, serving on Mingzong's staff.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was pleased with him and appointed him secretary on the Tianping military commission staff under Mingzong.

units.zh: 明宗歷汴、恒二鎮，皆隨府遷職。
units.en: Mingzong held the Bian and Heng commands in turn, and Wenju followed him in each transfer.
units.literal: Mingzong served the two commands of Bian and Heng; Wenju followed the headquarters in each transfer of post.

units.zh: 天成初，授右諫議大夫，知宣武軍軍州事，歷御史中丞、吏部侍郎、禮部尚書、西都副留守，判京兆府事，縱改兵部尚書。
units.en: At the start of Tiancheng he was appointed Right Remonstrance Councilor with charge of Xuanwu military and prefectural affairs, then served as censor-in-chief, vice minister of personnel, minister of rites, deputy protector of the western capital with concurrent administration of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture, and eventually minister of war.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was made Right Remonstrance Councilor and given charge of military and prefectural affairs of the Xuanwu Army; he served successively as Censor-in-Chief, Vice Minister of Personnel, Minister of Rites, Western Capital Deputy Protector, and concurrent administrator of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture, and was eventually made Minister of War.

units.zh: 文矩以嘗事霸府，每懷公輔之望。
units.en: Having once served in the founding ruler's headquarters, he always hoped for appointment as chief minister.
units.literal: Because Wenju had once served the hegemon's office, he always harbored hopes of becoming chief minister.

units.zh: 時高祖自外鎮入覲，嘗薦於明宗曰：「梁文矩早事陛下，甚有勤勞，未升相輔，外論慊之。」
units.en: When Gaozu came from a frontier command to pay court, he once said to Mingzong, "Liang Wenju served you early on with great diligence. He has not been made chief minister, and people outside the court feel the injustice of it."
units.literal: When Gaozu came from an outer command to pay court, he once recommended to Mingzong: "Liang Wenju served Your Majesty early and with great diligence; he has not been raised to chief minister, and public opinion resents it."

units.zh: 明宗曰：「久忘此人，吾之過也。」
units.en: Mingzong said, "I had forgotten him entirely—that was my fault."
units.literal: Mingzong said: "I had long forgotten this man—it is my fault."

units.zh: 尋有旨降命，會丁外憂而止。
units.en: An appointment edict was soon to follow, but the matter ended when he entered mourning for his father.
units.literal: Soon an edict was about to be issued, but it stopped when he entered mourning for his father.

units.zh: 清泰初，拜太常卿。
units.en: At the start of the Qingtai era he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 高祖即位，授吏部尚書，改太子少師。
units.en: When Gaozu came to the throne he was appointed minister of personnel, then made junior tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was made Minister of Personnel, then transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 文矩喜清靜之教，聚道書數千卷，企慕赤松、留侯之事，而服食尤盡其善。
units.en: Wenju embraced the Daoist ideal of stillness and purity, gathered several thousand volumes of Daoist texts, and looked up to the legends of Master Redpine and the Marquis of Liu. In dietary alchemy he pursued the art to its fullest.
units.literal: Wenju delighted in the teaching of stillness and purity, collected several thousand volumes of Daoist books, and yearned after the affairs of Chisong and the Marquis of Liu; in taking elixirs he especially pursued them to perfection.

units.zh: 後因風痹，上章請退，以太子太保致仕，居洛陽久之。
units.en: Later he developed rheumatism, submitted a memorial asking to retire, and left office as grand guardian of the heir apparent, living in Luoyang for many years.
units.literal: Later, because of wind paralysis, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and left office as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, residing long in Luoyang.

units.zh: 天福八年，以疾卒，時年五十九。
units.en: In the eighth Tianfu year he died of illness at the age of fifty-nine.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died of illness, aged fifty-nine.

units.zh: 贈太子太傅。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as grand tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 史圭，常山人也。
units.en: Shi Gui was a native of Changshan.
units.literal: Shi Gui was a man of Changshan.

units.zh: 其先與王武俊來於塞外，因家石邑。
units.en: His forebears had come from beyond the frontier with Wang Wujun and made their home in Shiyi.
units.literal: His ancestors came from beyond the frontier with Wang Wujun and settled their household in Shiyi.

units.zh: 高祖曾，歷鎮陽牙校。
units.en: His great-grandfather Zeng had served as a military clerk at Zhenyang.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Zeng had served as a military clerk at Zhenyang.

units.zh: 父鈞，假安平、九門令。
units.en: His father Jun had served as acting magistrate of Anping and Jiumen.
units.literal: His father Jun had been acting magistrate of Anping and Jiumen.

units.zh: 圭好學工詩，長於吏道。
units.en: Gui loved learning and wrote poetry well, and he excelled in administrative affairs.
units.literal: Gui loved learning and was skilled in poetry, excelling in the ways of administration.

units.zh: 唐光化中，歷阜城、饒陽尉，改房子、寧晉、元氏、樂壽、博陸五邑令。
units.en: During the Tang Guanghua era he served as assistant magistrate of Fucheng and Raoyang, then held successive magistracies in Fangzi, Ningjin, Yuanshi, Leshou, and Bolu.
units.literal: In the Guanghua era of Tang he served as assistant magistrate of Fucheng and Raoyang, then became magistrate in turn of the five districts of Fangzi, Ningjin, Yuanshi, Leshou, and Bolu.

units.zh: 為寧晉日，擅給驛廩，以貸饑民，民甚感之。
units.en: As magistrate of Ningjin he on his own authority opened the post-station granaries to lend grain to the starving, and the people were deeply grateful.
units.literal: While magistrate of Ningjin he on his own authority issued post-station grain stores to lend to famine victims; the people were deeply moved.

units.zh: 及為樂壽令，里人為之立碑。
units.en: When he became magistrate of Leshou, the local people erected a stele in his honor.
units.literal: When he became magistrate of Leshou, the villagers erected a stele for him.

units.zh: 同光中，任圜為真定尹，擢為本府司錄，不應命。
units.en: During the Tongguang era Ren Yuan was prefect of Zhending and offered Gui the post of prefectural recorder, but Gui declined.
units.literal: In the Tongguang era Ren Yuan was prefect of Zhending and promoted Gui to recorder of the prefecture, but he did not accept the appointment.

units.zh: 郭崇韜領其地，辟為從事，及明宗代崇韜，以舊職縻之。
units.en: Guo Chongtao governed the region and recruited him as an aide. When Mingzong replaced Chongtao he retained Gui in the same post.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao held that territory and recruited him as aide; when Mingzong replaced Chongtao he kept Gui in his former post.

units.zh: 明宗即位，入為文昌正郎，安重誨薦為河南少尹，判府事，尋命為樞密院直學士。
units.en: When Mingzong came to the throne Gui entered court as regular gentleman of Wenchang. An Chonghui recommended him as vice prefect of Henan with charge of prefectural affairs, and soon he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Gui entered court as Regular Gentleman of Wenchang. An Chonghui recommended him as Vice Prefect of Henan with concurrent administration of prefectural affairs, and soon he was appointed Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 時圭以受知於重誨，重誨奏令圭與同列閻至俱升殿侍立，以備顧問，明宗可之。
units.en: Gui had won Chonghui's confidence. Chonghui memorialized that Gui and his colleague Yan Zhi should both attend in the hall to stand ready for consultation, and Mingzong agreed.
units.literal: At that time Gui had won Chonghui's trust. Chonghui memorialized that Gui and his colleague Yan Zhi should both ascend the hall to attend and stand by, to be ready for consultation; Mingzong approved.

units.zh: 尋自左諫議大夫拜尚書右丞，有入相之望。
units.en: Soon he was promoted from Left Remonstrance Councilor to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and seemed headed for the chief ministership.
units.literal: Soon he was promoted from Left Remonstrance Councilor to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with prospects of entering the chief ministership.

units.zh: 圭敏於吏事，重誨本不知書，為事剛愎，每於明宗前可否重務，圭恬然終日，不能剖正其事。
units.en: Gui was quick in administrative matters, but Chonghui was unlearned and headstrong. Whenever Chonghui approved or rejected weighty matters before Mingzong, Gui would sit placidly all day without correcting him.
units.literal: Gui was sharp in administrative affairs, but Chonghui was by nature unlettered and obstinate in conduct. Whenever he approved or rejected weighty matters before Mingzong, Gui remained placid all day and could not set the affairs straight.

units.zh: 長興中，重誨既誅，圭出為貝州刺史，未幾罷免，退歸常山。
units.en: During the Changxing era, after Chonghui was executed, Gui was posted as prefect of Beizhou. Before long he was removed and retired to Changshan.
units.literal: In the Changxing era, after Chonghui was executed, Gui was sent out as Prefect of Beizhou; before long he was dismissed and retired to Changshan.

units.zh: 由是閉門杜絕人事，雖親戚故人造者不見其面，每遊別墅，則乘婦人氈車以自蔽匿，人莫知其心。
units.en: Thereafter he shut his doors to the world. Even kin and old friends who called on him could not see his face. When he visited his country estate he rode in a woman's covered cart to conceal himself, and no one could fathom his thoughts.
units.literal: Thereafter he shut his door and cut off all human contact; even when kin and old friends came calling he would not show his face. Whenever he visited his country villa he rode in a woman's felt cart to hide himself, and no one knew his mind.

units.zh: 高祖登極，征為刑部侍郎，判鹽鐵副使，皆宰臣馮道之奏請也。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne Gui was summoned as vice minister of justice and deputy commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly, all on Chief Minister Feng Dao's recommendation.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice and concurrent Deputy Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly—all on the memorial request of Chief Minister Feng Dao.

units.zh: 始圭在明宗時為右丞，權判銓事，道在中書，嘗以堂判衡銓司所註官，圭怒，力爭之，道亦微有不足之色，至是圭首為道所舉，方愧其度量遠不及也。
units.en: Earlier, when Gui was Right Vice Director under Mingzong with charge of selection affairs, Dao in the Secretariat had once used a chief minister's ruling to overturn the Selection Bureau's appointments. Gui had been furious and fought him hard; Dao too had shown displeasure. Now Gui was the first person Dao recommended, and he was ashamed to find how far Dao's magnanimity surpassed his own.
units.literal: Earlier, when Gui was Right Vice Director under Mingzong with acting charge of selection affairs, Dao was in the Secretariat and once used a chief-minister's ruling to overturn appointments registered by the Selection Bureau. Gui was angry and argued forcefully; Dao too showed a slight look of displeasure. Now Gui was the first whom Dao recommended, and he felt ashamed that his magnanimity fell far short.

units.zh: 旋改吏部侍郎，分知銓事，而圭素厲廉守節，大著公平之譽。
units.en: He was soon made vice minister of personnel with divided charge of selection affairs. Gui had always been strict in integrity, and he won wide renown for impartiality.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel with divided charge of selection affairs. Gui had always been strict in integrity and upholding principle, and won a great reputation for fairness.

units.zh: 圭前為河南少尹日，有嵩山術士遺圭石藥如鬥，謂圭曰：「服之可以延壽，然不可中輟，輟則疾作矣。」
units.en: When Gui had been vice prefect of Henan, a Mount Song adept gave him a stone elixir the size of a peck and said, "If you take this you may prolong your life, but you must not stop midway—if you stop, illness will follow."
units.literal: When Gui had earlier been Vice Prefect of Henan, a Mount Song adept gave him a stone elixir the size of a peck-measure and said: "If you take it you can prolong life, but you must not stop midway—if you stop, illness will arise."

units.zh: 圭後服之，神爽力健，深寶惜焉。
units.en: Gui later took it. His spirits were keen and his strength robust, and he treasured it deeply.
units.literal: Gui later took it; his spirit was clear and his strength robust, and he treasured it deeply.

units.zh: 清泰末，圭在常山，遇秘瓊之亂，時貯於衣笥，為賊所劫，後不復得。
units.en: At the end of the Qingtai era Gui was in Changshan when Mi Qiong's rebellion broke out. He had kept the elixir in a clothes chest, and bandits seized it. He never recovered it.
units.literal: At the end of Qingtai Gui was in Changshan when Mi Qiong's rebellion broke out. He had stored the elixir in his clothes chest; bandits plundered it and he never recovered it.

units.zh: 天福中，疾生胸臆之間，常如火灼，圭知不濟，求歸鄉里，詔許之。
units.en: During the Tianfu era illness settled in his chest, burning like fire. Gui knew he would not recover and asked to return home; the court granted his request.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era illness arose in his chest, often burning like fire. Gui knew he would not recover and requested return to his home district; an edict granted it.

units.zh: 及涉河，竟為藥氣所蒸，卒於路，歸葬石邑，時年六十八。
units.en: When he crossed the river he was overcome by the elixir's fumes and died on the road. He was buried in Shiyi at the age of sixty-eight.
units.literal: When he crossed the river he was at last overcome by the fumes of the elixir and died on the road. He was buried in Shiyi, aged sixty-eight.

units.zh: 裴皞，字司東，系出中眷裴氏，世居河東為望族。
units.en: Pei Hao, courtesy name Sidong, came from the central branch of the Pei clan and for generations his family had been a leading house in Hedong.
units.literal: Pei Hao, style name Sidong, was descended from the central branch of the Pei clan and for generations had dwelt in Hedong as an eminent family.

units.zh: 皞容止端秀，性卞急，剛直而無隱，少而好學，苦心文藝，雖遭亂離，手不釋卷。
units.en: Hao was handsome in bearing and deportment, quick-tempered, upright, and frank. From youth he loved learning and devoted himself to letters and the arts; even amid war and exile he never set his books aside.
units.literal: Hao's bearing and deportment were refined and handsome; his nature was quick-tempered, upright, and without concealment. From youth he loved learning and labored at letters and the arts; though he suffered turmoil and separation, he never let go his books.

units.zh: 唐光化三年，擢進士第，釋褐授校書郎，歷諫職。
units.en: In the third year of the Tang Guanghua era he passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering service he was appointed collator and later held remonstrance posts.
units.literal: In the third year of Guanghua of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon doffing commoner's clothes he was appointed collator and served in remonstrance posts.

units.zh: 梁初，當路推其文學，遷翰林學士、中書舍人。
units.en: Early in Liang those in power prized his literary talent, and he was made Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter.
units.literal: At the beginning of Liang those in power promoted his literary learning, and he was transferred to Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 唐莊宗時，擢為禮部侍郎，後以語觸當事，改太子賓客，旋授兵部尚書，以老致仕。
units.en: Under Tang Zhuangzong he was promoted to vice minister of rites. Later his words offended those in power and he was made guest of the heir apparent, then soon minister of war, and he retired on account of age.
units.literal: Under Tang Zhuangzong he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites; later his words offended those in power and he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent, then soon appointed Minister of War and retired on account of age.

units.zh: 天福初，起為工部尚書，復告老，以右僕射致仕。
units.en: At the start of Tianfu he was recalled as minister of works, again asked to retire, and left office as Right Vice Director.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he was recalled as Minister of Works, again requested retirement on account of age, and left office as Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 皞累知貢舉，稱得士，宰相馬裔孫、維翰皆其所取進士也。
units.en: Hao repeatedly supervised the civil service examinations and was praised for choosing worthy men; Chief Ministers Ma Yinsun and Sang Weihan were both jinshi he had advanced.
units.literal: Hao repeatedly supervised the civil service examinations and was said to have chosen worthy men; the chief ministers Ma Yinsun and Sang Weihan were both jinshi he had selected.

units.zh: 後裔孫知貢舉，率新進士謁皞，皞喜，為詩曰：「詞場最重是持衡，天遣愚夫受盛名，三主禮闈年八十，門生門下見門生。」
units.en: Later, when Yinsun supervised the examinations, he led the new jinshi to pay a call on Hao. Delighted, Hao composed a poem: "In the examination hall nothing matters more than holding the scales; Heaven sent this dull fellow to win great renown. Three times I presided over the ritual gate, now eighty years old—a student's student greets a student."
units.literal: Later when Yinsun supervised the examinations he led the new jinshi to visit Hao. Hao was delighted and composed a poem: "In the examination field nothing weighs more than holding the balance; Heaven sent this dull fellow to receive great fame. Three times I presided over the ritual gate, now eighty years old—a student's student sees a student."

units.zh: 當世榮之。
units.en: His contemporaries admired him for it.
units.literal: The age honored him for it.

units.zh: 維翰嘗私見皞，皞不為迎送，人問之，皞曰：「我見桑公於中書，庶僚也；
units.en: Weihan once called on Hao in private, but Hao did not go out to welcome or escort him. When people asked why, Hao said, "When I saw Lord Sang at the Secretariat, he was a colleague among officials;
units.literal: Weihan once paid a private visit to Hao, but Hao did not go out to welcome or see him off. When people asked about it, Hao said: "When I saw Lord Sang at the Secretariat, he was a fellow official;

units.zh: 今見我於私第，門生也。」
units.en: but now he visits me at home—he is my student."
units.literal: now he comes to see me at my private residence—he is a student."

units.zh: 聞者以為允。
units.en: Those who heard it agreed he was right.
units.literal: Those who heard it thought it apt.

units.zh: 卒年八十五。
units.en: He died at the age of eighty-five.
units.literal: He died at the age of eighty-five.

units.zh: 贈太子太保。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as grand guardian of the heir apparent.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 吳承範，字表微，魏州人也。
units.en: Wu Chengfan, courtesy name Biaowei, was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Wu Chengfan, style name Biaowei, was a man of Weizhou.

units.zh: 父瓊，右金吾衛將軍，累贈太子少保。
units.en: His father Qiong was general of the Right Gold Crow Guard and was posthumously honored on successive occasions as junior guardian of the heir apparent.
units.literal: His father Qiong was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard and was repeatedly posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 承範少好學，善屬文，唐閔帝之鎮鄴都也，聞其才名，署為賓職，承範懇求隨計，閔帝許之。
units.en: From youth Chengfan loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. When the Tang Emperor Min was stationed at Yedu, he heard of Chengfan's talent and reputation and appointed him as a guest official. Chengfan earnestly asked to accompany him on the tribute journey to the capital, and Emperor Min agreed.
units.literal: Chengfan from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. When the Tang Emperor Min was posted at Yedu, he heard of Chengfan's talent and reputation and appointed him as a guest official. Chengfan earnestly requested to accompany him on the tribute journey, and Emperor Min permitted it.

units.zh: 長興三年春，擢進士第。
units.en: In spring of the third year of Changxing he passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: In spring of the third year of Changxing, he was selected as a jinshi.

units.zh: 及閔帝即位，授左拾遺。
units.en: When Emperor Min took the throne, he was appointed Left Reminder.
units.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, he was appointed Left Reminder.

units.zh: 清泰二年，以本官充史館修撰，與同職張昭遠等共修《明宗實錄》，轉右補闕，依前充職。
units.en: In the second year of Qingtai, while retaining his existing post he was made compiler at the Historiography Institute and, together with fellow compiler Zhang Zhaoyuan and others, jointly compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Mingzong. He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and continued in the same office.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai, in his existing capacity he was made Compiler at the Historiography Institute and together with fellow compiler Zhang Zhaoyuan and others jointly compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Mingzong. He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and continued in his former office.

units.zh: 高祖革命，遷尚書屯田員外郎、知制誥。
units.en: When Gaozu founded the dynasty, he was promoted to vice director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts.
units.literal: When Gaozu founded the new dynasty, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and Drafter of Edicts.

units.zh: 天福三年，改樞密院直學士，未幾，自祠部郎中、知制誥召充翰林學士，正拜中書舍人，賜金紫。
units.en: In the third year of Tianfu he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafter of edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, formally appointed Secretariat drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianfu he was changed to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and Drafter of Edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician, formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，遷禮部侍郎，知貢舉，尋遘疾而卒，年四十二。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was promoted to vice minister of rites and placed in charge of the examinations. Soon after he fell ill and died at the age of forty-two.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the examinations. Soon after he fell ill and died, aged forty-two.

units.zh: 贈工部尚書。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as minister of works.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.

units.zh: 承範溫厚寡言，善希人旨，桑維翰、李崧尤重之，嘗薦於高祖，雲可大用。
units.en: Wu Chengfan was gentle and sparing of words, adept at reading others' wishes. Sang Weihan and Li Song held him in special regard and once recommended him to Gaozu as fit for high office.
units.literal: Chengfan was mild and reticent, skilled at discerning others' intent. Sang Weihan and Li Song especially valued him and once recommended him to Gaozu, saying he could be greatly employed.

units.zh: 承範知之，持重自養，雖遇盛夏，而猶服襦袴，加之以純綿，蓋慮有寒濕之患也。
units.en: Chengfan understood this and kept himself in careful reserve. Even in midsummer he still wore jacket and trousers lined with cotton, lest he suffer from cold and damp.
units.literal: Chengfan knew this and cultivated himself with restraint. Even in midsummer he still wore jacket and trousers with pure cotton added, fearing ailments from cold and damp.

units.zh: 然竟不獲其志，其命也夫！
units.en: Yet in the end he never attained his ambition—such was fate!
units.literal: Yet in the end he did not realize his ambition—such was his fate!

units.zh: 盧導，字熙化，其先范陽人也。
units.en: Lu Dao, courtesy name Xihua, came originally from Fanyang.
units.literal: Lu Dao, style name Xihua, was originally from Fanyang.

units.zh: 祖伯卿，唐殿中侍御史。
units.en: His grandfather Boqing served as attending censor in the palace under Tang.
units.literal: His grandfather Boqing was Attending Censor in the Palace of Tang.

units.zh: 父如晦，國子監丞，贈戶部侍郎。
units.en: His father Ruhui was assistant director of the Directorate of Education and was posthumously honored as vice minister of revenue.
units.literal: His father Ruhui was Assistant Director of the Directorate of Education and was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 導少而儒雅，美詞翰，善談論。
units.en: From youth Dao was cultivated and scholarly, gifted in letters, and an engaging speaker.
units.literal: Dao from youth was refined and scholarly, excelled in letters, and was skilled in discourse.

units.zh: 唐天祐初，登進士第，釋褐除校書郎，由均州鄖鄉縣令、入為監察御史，三遷職方員外郎，充史館修撰，改河南縣令禮部郎中，賜紫，轉右司郎中兼侍御史知雜事。
units.en: At the start of the Tang Tianyou era he passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering service he was appointed collator, then magistrate of Yunxiang in Jun Prefecture, then investigating censor at court. After three promotions he became vice director of the Bureau of Appointments and compiler in the History Office, then magistrate of Henan and director of the Ministry of Rites, received purple robes, and became right department director while also serving as attending censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon doffing commoner's clothes he was made collator, then magistrate of Yunxiang in Jun Prefecture, then entered court as Investigating Censor. After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments, served as compiler in the History Office, was changed to magistrate of Henan and Director of the Ministry of Rites, was granted purple robes, and became Right Department Director concurrently Attending Censor in charge of Miscellaneous Affairs.

units.zh: 以病免，閑居於漢上，久之。
units.en: Illness forced his retirement, and he lived in seclusion along the Han for many years.
units.literal: He was dismissed on account of illness and lived in retirement on the Han River for a long time.

units.zh: 天成中，以本官征還，拜右諫議大夫。
units.en: During the Tiancheng era he was recalled to his former rank and appointed Right Remonstrance Councilor.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was recalled in his former rank and appointed Right Remonstrance Councilor.

units.zh: 長興末，為中書舍人，權知貢舉。
units.en: At the end of the Changxing era he was Secretariat drafter with acting charge of the civil service examinations.
units.literal: At the end of Changxing he was Secretariat Drafter with acting charge of the civil service examinations.

units.zh: 明年春，潞王自鳳翔擁大軍赴闕，唐閔帝奔於衛州，宰相馮道、李愚集百官於天宮寺，將出迎潞王。
units.en: The following spring the Prince of Lu led a great army from Fengxiang toward the capital. Emperor Min of Tang fled to Weizhou. Chief ministers Feng Dao and Li Yu assembled the officials at Tiangong Temple, preparing to go out and welcome the prince.
units.literal: The next spring the Prince of Lu marched from Fengxiang at the head of a great army toward the capital. Tang Emperor Min fled to Weizhou. Chief ministers Feng Dao and Li Yu gathered the officials at Tiangong Temple, intending to go out and welcome the Prince of Lu.

units.zh: 時軍眾離潰，人情奔駭，百官移時未有至者。
units.en: The armies were scattered in rout and the people fled in panic. For a long while no officials appeared.
units.literal: At the time the armies were scattered in rout and the people fled in panic; for a long while no officials arrived.

units.zh: 導與舍人張昭遠先至，馮道請導草勸進箋，導曰：「潞王入朝，郊迎可也；
units.en: Dao and Drafter Zhang Zhaoyuan arrived first. Feng Dao asked Dao to draft a memorial urging the prince to take the throne. Dao said, "When the Prince of Lu comes to court, a suburban welcome is enough;
units.literal: Dao and Drafter Zhang Zhaoyuan arrived first. Feng Dao asked Dao to draft a memorial urging accession. Dao said: "When the Prince of Lu enters court, a suburban welcome is fitting;

units.zh: 若勸進之事，安可造次。
units.en: as for urging him to take the throne, how can we do that rashly.
units.literal: as for urging accession, how can it be done rashly.

units.zh: 且潞王與主上，皆太后之子，或廢或立，當從教令，安得不稟策母後，率爾而行！」
units.en: Moreover, the prince and the emperor are both sons of the Empress Dowager. Whether one is deposed or enthroned should follow her command. How can we act without seeking her decision and proceed so recklessly!"
units.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Lu and the emperor are both sons of the Empress Dowager. Whether one is deposed or enthroned should follow her command—how can we act without seeking the Empress Dowager's decision and proceed so lightly!"

units.zh: 馮道曰：「凡事要務實，勸進其可已乎？」
units.en: Feng Dao said, "In all affairs one must be practical. Can we stop short of urging accession?"
units.literal: Feng Dao said: "In all affairs one must be practical—can urging accession be stopped?"

units.zh: 導曰：「今主上蒙塵在外，遽以大位勸人，若潞王守道，以忠義見責，未審何詞以對！
units.en: Dao said, "The emperor now suffers exile abroad. If we hastily offer the throne to another, and the prince holds to loyalty and rebukes us for treachery, what answer could we give?
units.literal: Dao said: "Now the emperor suffers exile abroad. If we hastily urge the throne upon another, and the Prince of Lu holds to the Way and rebukes us for disloyalty, I do not know what words we could answer with!

units.zh: 不如率群臣詣宮門，取太后進止，即去就善矣。」
units.en: Better to lead the ministers to the palace gate and obtain the Empress Dowager's decision. Then whether to go or stay will be properly settled."
units.literal: It would be better to lead the ministers to the palace gate and obtain the Empress Dowager's decision—then whether to go or stay would be well settled."

units.zh: 道未及對，會京城巡檢安從進報曰：「潞王至矣，安得百僚無班。」
units.en: Before Dao could reply, capital inspector An Congjin reported, "The Prince of Lu has arrived. How can the officials stand without order."
units.literal: Before Dao could reply, Capital Inspector An Congjin reported: "The Prince of Lu has arrived—how can the officials be without formation."

units.zh: 即紛然而去。
units.en: Everyone scattered and hurried away.
units.literal: They at once scattered and left.

units.zh: 是日，潞王未至，馮道等止於上陽門外，又令導草勸進箋，導執之如初。
units.en: That day the prince had not yet arrived. Feng Dao and the others waited outside the Shangyang Gate and again ordered Dao to draft the accession memorial. Dao held firm as before.
units.literal: That day the Prince of Lu had not yet arrived; Feng Dao and the others stopped outside the Shangyang Gate and again ordered Dao to draft the accession memorial. Dao held to his position as before.

units.zh: 李愚曰：「舍人之言是也，吾輩信罪人矣。」
units.en: Li Yu said, "The drafter is right. We are truly guilty men."
units.literal: Li Yu said: "The drafter's words are right—we are indeed guilty men."

units.zh: 導之守正也如是。
units.en: Such was Dao's steadfast integrity.
units.literal: Such was Dao's upholding of what was right.

units.zh: 晉天福中，由禮部侍郎遷尚書右丞，判吏部尚書銓事，秩滿，拜吏部侍郎。
units.en: During the Jin Tianfu era he rose from vice minister of rites to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with charge of selection affairs under the minister of personnel. When his term ended he was made vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he was transferred from Vice Minister of Rites to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent administration of selection affairs under the Minister of Personnel; when his term ended he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 六年秋，卒於東京，時年七十六。
units.en: In the autumn of the sixth year he died in the Eastern Capital at the age of seventy-six.
units.literal: In autumn of the sixth year he died in the Eastern Capital, aged seventy-six.

units.zh: 鄭韜光，字龍府，洛京清河人也。
units.en: Zheng Taoguang, courtesy name Longfu, was a native of Qinghe in the Luoyang capital region.
units.literal: Zheng Taoguang, style name Longfu, was a man of Qinghe in the Luoyang capital region.

units.zh: 曾祖絪，為唐宰相。
units.en: His great-grandfather Yin served as a Tang chief minister.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Yin was a chief minister of Tang.

units.zh: 祖祗德，國子祭酒，
units.en: His grandfather Zhide was chancellor of the Directorate of Education,
units.literal: His grandfather Zhide was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世系表》：祗德，兵部尚書。）〉
units.en: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers by Clan: Zhide was minister of war.)
units.literal: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers by Clan: Zhide was Minister of War.)〉

units.zh: 贈太傅。
units.en: and was posthumously honored as grand tutor.
units.literal: and was posthumously awarded Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 父顥，河南尹，贈太師。
units.en: His father Hao was prefect of Henan and was posthumously honored as grand preceptor.
units.literal: His father Hao was Prefect of Henan and was posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 其先世居滎陽，自隋、唐三百餘年，公卿輔相，蟬聯一門。
units.en: His forebears had long lived in Xingyang. For more than three hundred years from Sui through Tang, chief ministers and high officials had followed one another in a single clan.
units.literal: His ancestors had long dwelt in Xingyang; for more than three hundred years from Sui through Tang, high ministers and chief councilors had followed one another in a single clan.

units.zh: 韜光，唐宣宗之外孫，萬壽公主之所出也，生三日，賜一子出身，銀章朱紱。
units.en: Taoguang was a maternal grandson of Tang Emperor Xuānzong, born to Princess Wanshou. On the third day after his birth he was granted hereditary office status, with silver seal and crimson tassel.
units.literal: Taoguang was a grandson of Tang Emperor Xuanzong on the maternal side, born to Princess Wanshou. On the third day after his birth he was granted the status of a son who enters office, with silver seal and crimson tassel.

units.zh: 及長，美容止，神爽氣澈，不妄喜怒，秉執名節，為甲族所稱。
units.en: As he grew he had a handsome bearing, a clear and spirited presence, showed anger or joy only with reason, and upheld reputation and principle, winning praise from the great families.
units.literal: When he grew up he had fine bearing, a clear spirit and transparent air, did not show anger or joy lightly, and upheld reputation and principle, and was praised by the leading clans.

units.zh: 自京兆府參軍歷秘書郎、集賢校理、太常博士、虞部比部員外郎、司門戶部郎中、河南京兆少尹、太常少卿、諫議大夫、給事中。
units.en: He rose from aide in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture through secretary, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, vice director in the bureaus of parks and review, director in the bureau of passes and the Ministry of Revenue, vice prefect of Henan and Jingzhao, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, remonstrance councilor, and attendant.
units.literal: From aide in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture he served successively as secretary, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, vice director in the Bureau of Parks and the Bureau of Review, director in the Bureau of Passes and the Ministry of Revenue, vice prefect of Henan and Jingzhao, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, remonstrance councilor, and attendant.

units.zh: 梁貞明中，懇求休退，上表漏名，責授寧州司馬。
units.en: During the Liang Zhenming era he earnestly sought to retire. His memorial omitted his name, and he was demoted to military adjutant of Ning Prefecture.
units.literal: In the Zhenming era of Liang he earnestly sought retirement; his memorial omitted his name and he was punished by appointment as military adjutant of Ning Prefecture.

units.zh: 莊宗平梁，遷工、禮、刑部侍郎。
units.en: When Zhuangzong conquered Liang he served in succession as vice minister of works, rites, and justice.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong conquered Liang he was transferred to vice minister of works, rites, and justice in succession.

units.zh: 天成、長興中，歷尚書左右丞。
units.en: During the Tiancheng and Changxing eras he served in turn as left and right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng and Changxing eras he served in turn as Left and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 國初，以戶部尚書致仕。
units.en: At the founding of the dynasty he retired as minister of revenue.
units.literal: At the founding of the state he retired as Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 自繈褓迄於懸車，凡事十一君，越七十載，所仕無官謗，無私過，三持使節，不辱君命，士無賢不肖，皆恭己接納。
units.en: From infancy to retirement he served eleven rulers over more than seventy years. In every post he earned no reproach and committed no private wrong. Three times he bore diplomatic credentials and never failed his sovereign's trust. Worthy or unworthy, he received every visitor with respectful courtesy.
units.literal: From swaddling clothes to hanging up his carriage, he served eleven rulers over more than seventy years. In office he incurred no blame for his posts and no private fault. Three times he bore diplomatic credentials and never disgraced his sovereign's charge. Whether a man was worthy or not, he received all with respectful courtesy.

units.zh: 晚年背傴，時人咸曰鄭傴不迂。
units.en: In old age his back was bent, and people said, "Bent-back Zheng is not stubborn."
units.literal: In his later years his back was bent, and people of the time all said, "Bent-back Zheng is not obstinate."

units.zh: 平生交友之中無怨隙，親族之間無愛憎，恬和自如，性尚平簡，及致政歸洛，甚愜終焉之志。
units.en: He bore no grudges among lifelong friends and showed no favoritism among kin. Tranquil and at ease, he loved simplicity. When he retired and returned to Luoyang he was deeply content to end his days there.
units.literal: Among friends of a lifetime he bore no rancor; among kin he showed no favor or dislike. He was tranquil and at ease, by nature inclined to simplicity, and when he left office and returned to Luoyang he was very content with his wish to end his days there.

units.zh: 天福五年秋，寢疾而卒，年八十。
units.en: In the autumn of the fifth Tianfu year he fell ill in bed and died at the age of eighty.
units.literal: In autumn of the fifth year of Tianfu he took to his bed with illness and died, aged eighty.

units.zh: 贈右僕射。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 王權，字秀山，太原人，積世衣冠。
units.en: Wang Quan, courtesy name Xiushan, was a native of Taiyuan from a long line of officials.
units.literal: Wang Quan, style name Xiushan, was a man of Taiyuan from a family of officials for generations.

units.zh: 曾祖起，官至左僕射、山南西道節度使，冊贈太尉，謚曰文懿，唐史有傳。
units.en: His great-grandfather Qi rose to Left Vice Director and military commissioner of the Shannan West circuit, was posthumously honored as grand marshal with the posthumous title Wenyi, and has a biography in the Tang histories.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Qi rose to Left Vice Director and military commissioner of the Shannan West circuit; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal with the posthumous title Weny, and has a biography in the Tang histories.

units.zh: 祖龜，浙東觀察使。
units.en: His grandfather Gui was observation commissioner of Zhedong.
units.literal: His grandfather Gui was observation commissioner of Zhedong.

units.zh: 父蕘，右司員外郎。
units.en: His father Rao was vice director of the Right Department.
units.literal: His father Rao was Vice Director of the Right Department.

units.zh: 權舉進士，解褐授秘書省校書郎、集賢校理，歷左拾遺、右補闕。
units.en: Quan passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering service he was appointed collator in the Secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then served as Left and Right Reminder.
units.literal: Quan passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office robes he was appointed collator in the Secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and served as Left and Right Reminder.

units.zh: 梁祖革命，御史司憲崔沂表為侍御史，遷兼職方員外郎知雜事。
units.en: When the Liang founder seized power, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yi recommended him as attending censor. He was promoted to concurrent vice director of the Bureau of Appointments with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
units.literal: When the Liang founder changed the dynasty, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yi memorialized him as Attending Censor; he was promoted to concurrent Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments with charge of miscellaneous affairs.

units.zh: 歲餘，召入翰林為學士，在院加戶部郎中、知制誥，歷左諫議大夫、給事中，充集賢殿學士判院事，俄拜御史中丞。
units.en: After a year he was called into the Hanlin as academician, additionally made director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of drafting edicts, then Left Remonstrance Councilor and attendant, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy, and soon censor-in-chief.
units.literal: After more than a year he was summoned to the Hanlin as academician; while in the academy he was additionally made Director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of drafting edicts, served as Left Remonstrance Councilor and Attendant, was made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy, and soon was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，以例出為隨州司馬，會赦，量移許州。
units.en: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang he was demoted under precedent to military adjutant of Suizhou. An amnesty followed and he was transferred in reduced rank to Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang he was demoted by precedent to military adjutant of Suizhou; an amnesty came and he was transferred in reduced rank to Xuzhou.

units.zh: 月餘，入為右庶子，遷戶兵吏三侍郎、尚書左丞、禮部尚書判銓。
units.en: After a month he entered court as Right Household Companion, then rose through the vice ministries of revenue, war, and personnel, became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and minister of rites with charge of selection.
units.literal: After more than a month he entered court as Right Household Companion, then was transferred through the three vice ministries of revenue, war, and personnel, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Minister of Rites with charge of selection.

units.zh: 清泰中，權知貢舉，改戶部尚書，華資美級，罕不由之。
units.en: During the Qingtai era he had acting charge of the examinations and was made minister of revenue. Few splendid qualifications and fine ranks did not pass through his hands.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he had acting charge of the examinations and was changed to Minister of Revenue. Splendid qualifications and fine ranks rarely did not pass through his hands.

units.zh: 高祖登極，轉兵部尚書。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was made minister of war.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was transferred to Minister of War.

units.zh: 天福中，命權使於契丹，權以前世累為將相，未嘗有奉使而稱陪臣者，謂人曰：「我雖不才，年今耄矣，豈能遠使於契丹乎！
units.en: During the Tianfu era Quan was ordered to serve as envoy to the Khitan. His forebears for generations had been generals and chief ministers, yet none had ever been sent abroad to be called a subordinate minister. He told others, "Though I lack talent, I am old now. How could I go on a distant mission to the Khitan?
units.literal: In the Tianfu era Quan was ordered to serve as envoy to the Khitan. Quan, whose forebears for generations had been generals and chief ministers, had never seen one sent on mission who was called a subordinate minister. He said to others: "Though I lack talent, I am now old—how could I go on a distant mission to the Khitan!

units.zh: 違詔得罪，亦所甘心。」
units.en: To disobey the edict and accept punishment is something I would willingly bear."
units.literal: To disobey the edict and incur punishment is also what I would willingly accept."

units.zh: 由是停任。
units.en: The appointment was therefore suspended.
units.literal: For this the appointment was suspended.

units.zh: 先是，宰相馮道使於契丹才回，權亦自鳳翔冊禮使回，故責詞略曰：「若以道路迢遙，即鸞閣之臺臣亦往；
units.en: Chief Minister Feng Dao had just returned from an embassy to the Khitan, and Quan had just returned from Fengxiang as investiture envoy. The reprimand therefore read in part, "If the road is long and distant, ministers of the Phoenix Pavilion also travel;
units.literal: Earlier Chief Minister Feng Dao had just returned from an embassy to the Khitan, and Quan had also just returned from Fengxiang as envoy for investiture rites. Therefore the reprimand read in part: "If the road is far and distant, then ministers of the Phoenix Pavilion also go;

units.zh: 若以筋骸衰減，即鳳翔之冊使才回。
units.en: if one's body is weakened with age, the investiture envoy from Fengxiang has just returned.
units.literal: if the sinews and bones are weakened with age, then the investiture envoy from Fengxiang has just returned.

units.zh: 既黷憲章，須從殿黜」云。
units.en: Having violated the statutes, he must be demoted from court," and so forth.
units.literal: Having violated the statutes, he must be demoted from the hall," and so on.

units.zh: 其實權不欲臣事契丹，故堅辭之，非避事以違命也。
units.en: In truth Quan did not wish to serve the Khitan as a subject, and therefore firmly declined. He was not merely shirking duty to disobey orders.
units.literal: In truth Quan did not wish to serve the Khitan as a subject, and therefore firmly declined; it was not that he shirked duty to disobey orders.

units.zh: 逾歲授太子少傅致仕。
units.en: After more than a year he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent and retired.
units.literal: After more than a year he was granted Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

units.zh: 六年秋，以疾卒，年七十八。
units.en: In the autumn of the sixth year he died of illness at the age of seventy-eight.
units.literal: In autumn of the sixth year he died of illness, aged seventy-eight.

units.zh: 贈左僕射。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 韓惲，字子重，太原晉陽人。
units.en: Han Yun, courtesy name Zizhong, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Han Yun, style name Zizhong, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 曾祖俊，唐龍武大將軍。
units.en: His great-grandfather Jun was grand general of the Tang Dragon Martial Guard.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Jun was Grand General of the Tang Dragon Martial Guard.

units.zh: 祖士則，石州司馬。
units.en: His grandfather Shize was military adjutant of Shi Prefecture.
units.literal: His grandfather Shize was military adjutant of Shi Prefecture.

units.zh: 父逵，代州刺史。
units.en: His father Kui was prefect of Dai Prefecture.
units.literal: His father Kui was Prefect of Dai Prefecture.

units.zh: 惲世仕太原，昆仲為軍職，惟惲親狎儒士，好為歌詩，聚書數千卷。
units.en: The Han family had served at Taiyuan for generations. His brothers held military posts, but Yun alone kept company with scholars, loved to write songs and poems, and collected several thousand books.
units.literal: The Han family for generations served at Taiyuan; his brothers held military posts, but Yun alone was intimate with scholars, loved to compose songs and poems, and collected several thousand volumes of books.

units.zh: 乾寧中，後唐莊宗納其妹為妃，初為嫡室，故莊宗深禮其家，而惲以文學署交城、文水令，入為太原少尹。
units.en: During the Qianning era Zhuangzong of Later Tang took Yun's younger sister as consort. She was at first his principal wife, so Zhuangzong treated the family with great respect. Yun was appointed by literary merit magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui, then became vice prefect of Taiyuan.
units.literal: In the Qianning era Later Tang Zhuangzong took Yun's younger sister as consort; she was at first the principal wife, so Zhuangzong treated the family with deep courtesy. Yun was appointed by literary merit magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui, then entered service as Vice Prefect of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 莊宗平定趙、魏，為魏州支使。
units.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei, Yun served as branch commissioner of Weizhou.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei, Yun served as branch commissioner of Weizhou.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，授右散騎常侍，從駕至洛陽，轉尚書戶部侍郎。
units.en: When Zhuangzong came to the throne Yun was appointed Right Regular Attendant, accompanied the court to Luoyang, and was made vice minister of revenue in the Secretariat.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne Yun was appointed Right Regular Attendant, followed the imperial carriage to Luoyang, and was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 天成初，改秘書監。
units.en: At the start of the Tiancheng era he was made director of the Palace Library.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was changed to Director of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 俄而馮道為丞相，與惲有同幕之舊，以惲性謹厚，尤左右之，尋遷禮部尚書。
units.en: Soon Feng Dao became chief minister. He and Yun had served on the same staff long before. Feng especially favored Yun for his careful and honest nature, and soon Yun was made minister of rites.
units.literal: Soon Feng Dao became chief minister; he and Yun had old ties from the same staff. Because Yun was careful and honest, Feng especially favored him, and soon he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 丁內憂，服闋，授戶部尚書。
units.en: After mourning for his mother he was appointed minister of revenue.
units.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 明宗晏駕，馮道為山陵使，引惲為副使。
units.en: When Mingzong died Feng Dao was commissioner for the imperial tomb and appointed Yun his deputy.
units.literal: When Mingzong died Feng Dao was commissioner for the imperial tomb and brought Yun in as deputy commissioner.

units.zh: 清泰初，以充奉之勞，授檢校尚書右僕射、絳州刺史，逾年入為太子賓客。
units.en: At the start of the Qingtai era, for his service at the funeral, he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Jiang Prefecture. After a year he entered court as guest of the heir apparent.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, for his labor in the funeral service, he was appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prefect of Jiang Prefecture; after more than a year he entered court as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 高祖登極，以惲先朝懿戚，深加禮遇，除授貝州刺史。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he treated Yun with special courtesy as a kinsman of the former court and appointed him prefect of Bei Prefecture.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, because Yun was a kinsman by marriage of the former court, he treated him with deep courtesy and appointed him Prefect of Bei Prefecture.

units.zh: 時範延光有跋扈之狀，惲懼其見逼，遲留不敢赴任，高祖不悅，復授太子賓客，尋改兵部尚書。
units.en: Fan Yanguang was then acting insubordinately. Yun feared being caught in his power, lingered, and dared not take up the post. Gaozu was displeased, made him guest of the heir apparent again, and soon minister of war.
units.literal: At the time Fan Yanguang showed signs of insubordination. Yun feared being pressed by him, delayed and dared not take up the post. Gaozu was displeased, again appointed him Guest of the Heir Apparent, and soon changed him to Minister of War.

units.zh: 天福七年夏，車駕在鄴，惲病腳氣，卒於龍興寺，時年六十餘。
units.en: In the summer of the seventh Tianfu year the court was at Ye. Yun suffered from beriberi and died at Longxing Temple, aged over sixty.
units.literal: In summer of the seventh year of Tianfu the imperial carriage was at Ye. Yun suffered from foot ailment and died at Longxing Temple, aged over sixty.

units.zh: 李懌，京兆人也。
units.en: Li Yi was a native of Jingzhao.
units.literal: Li Yi was a man of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 祖褒，唐黔南觀察使。
units.en: His grandfather Bao was observation commissioner of Qiannan under Tang.
units.literal: His grandfather Bao was observation commissioner of Qiannan in Tang.

units.zh: 父昭，戶部尚書。
units.en: His father Zhao was minister of revenue.
units.literal: His father Zhao was Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 懌幼而能文，進士擢第，解褐為校書郎、集賢校理、清河尉。
units.en: Yi could write from childhood. He passed the jinshi examination and upon entering service became collator, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and assistant magistrate of Qinghe.
units.literal: Yi from youth could write; he passed the jinshi examination and upon first donning official robes was collator, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and assistant magistrate of Qinghe.

units.zh: 入梁，歷監察御史、右補闕、殿中侍御史、起居舍人、禮部員外郎、知制誥，換都官郎中，賜緋，召入翰林為學士，正拜舍人，賜金紫，仍舊內職。
units.en: Under Liang he served in succession as investigating censor, Right Reminder, attending censor in the palace, diarist, vice director of the Ministry of Rites with charge of drafting edicts, then director of the Bureau of Justice. He received crimson robes, was called into the Hanlin as academician, formally appointed drafter, granted gold seal and purple robes, and kept his inner-court duties.
units.literal: Entering Liang he served successively as Investigating Censor, Right Reminder, Attending Censor in the Palace, Diarist, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites with charge of drafting edicts, then Director of the Bureau of Justice, was granted crimson robes, was summoned to the Hanlin as academician, formally appointed drafter, granted gold seal and purple robes, and retained his inner-court duties.

units.zh: 莊宗平汴、洛，責授懷州司馬，遇赦，量移孟州，入為衛尉少卿。
units.en: When Zhuangzong conquered Bian and Luoyang, Yi was demoted to military adjutant of Huaizhou. An amnesty followed and he was transferred in reduced rank to Meng Prefecture, then entered court as vice director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong conquered Bian and Luo, Yi was punished by appointment as military adjutant of Huaizhou; an amnesty came and he was transferred in reduced rank to Meng Prefecture, then entered court as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

units.zh: 天成初，復拜中書舍人，充翰林學士，在職轉戶部侍郎右丞，充承旨。
units.en: At the start of the Tiancheng era he was again made Secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician, then vice minister of revenue and Right Vice Director while serving as chief drafter.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was again appointed Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician; while in office he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and Right Vice Director, and served as Chief Drafter.

units.zh: 時常侍張文寶知貢舉，中書奏落進士數人，仍請詔翰林學士院作一詩一賦，下禮部，為舉人格樣。
units.en: Attendant Zhang Wenbao then had charge of the examinations. The Secretariat memorialized to fail several jinshi and asked that the Hanlin Academy draft one poem and one fu for the Ministry of Rites as models for candidates.
units.literal: At the time Attendant Zhang Wenbao had charge of the examinations. The Secretariat memorialized to fail several jinshi and also requested an edict that the Hanlin Academy draft one poem and one fu to send down to the Ministry of Rites as models for candidates.

units.zh: 學士竇夢徵、張礪輩撰格詩格賦各一，送中書，宰相未以為允。
units.en: Academicians Dou Mengzheng, Zhang Li, and others each drafted a model poem and model fu and sent them to the Secretariat, but the chief ministers did not approve them.
units.literal: Academicians Dou Mengzheng, Zhang Li, and others each drafted a model poem and model fu and sent them to the Secretariat; the chief ministers did not approve them.

units.zh: 夢徵等請懌為之，懌笑而答曰：「李懌識字有數，頃歲因人偶得及第，敢與後生髦俊為之標格！
units.en: Mengzheng and the others asked Yi to do it. Yi smiled and said, "Li Yi knows only so many characters. A few years ago I passed the examination only by chance through others' help. How dare I set the standard for the brilliant young men of today!
units.literal: Mengzheng and the others asked Yi to do it. Yi smiled and answered: "Li Yi knows only so many characters. A few years ago I happened to pass the examination through others' help—how dare I set the standard for the brilliant young men of later generations!

units.zh: 假令今卻稱進士，就春官求試，落第必矣。
units.en: If I were called a jinshi today and went to the spring office for examination, I would certainly fail.
units.literal: If I were called a jinshi today and went to the spring office to seek examination, I would certainly fail.

units.zh: 格賦格詩，不敢應詔。」
units.en: As for the model fu and model poem, he dared not obey the edict."
units.literal: As for the model fu and model poem, he dared not comply with the edict."

units.zh: 君子多其識大體。
units.en: Men of judgment praised him for seeing what truly mattered.
units.literal: Men of virtue praised him for recognizing the larger principle.

units.zh: 天福中，自工部尚書轉太常卿，歷禮部、刑部二尚書，以多病留司於洛下，不交人事。
units.en: During the Tianfu era he rose from minister of works to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then served as minister of rites and minister of justice. Because of chronic illness he remained on duty in Luoyang and kept aloof from worldly affairs.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era he was transferred from Minister of Works to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served as Ministers of Rites and Justice in succession, and because of many illnesses remained on duty in Luoyang without engaging in worldly affairs.

units.zh: 開運未，遇契丹入洛，家事罄空，尋以疾卒，年七十餘。
units.en: Near the end of the Kaiyun era, when the Khitan entered Luoyang, his household was stripped bare. Soon he died of illness, aged over seventy.
units.literal: Near the end of Kaiyun, when the Khitan entered Luoyang, his household was emptied; soon he died of illness, aged over seventy.
